# Results — Study 72 (Loaded-Dice) on real 5-minute tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — SMA(5)/SMA(10)
crossover on 5-minute bars, enter at the next bar's open **in the direction of the cross**,
exit on a symmetric take-profit/stop of **±1 ATR(20)**, flat at the 16:00 ET close — run across a
basket of eight liquid instruments and pinned against a **random-direction control** on the
*same* entries. RTH 09:30–16:00 ET. As-of **2026-06-12**; Yahoo serves only ~60 calendar days of
5-minute bars, so the window is a rolling span ending ~now — match the per-tape fingerprint to
confirm you hold the same tape. Trades pooled across the basket: **n = 3,801** (~11.3/instrument/day).*

## The honest test — symmetric ±1 ATR, gross (cost = 0)

A direction-symmetric payoff is the only fair way to ask *"does the cross point the right way?"*
— with TP and SL equidistant, a coin earns ≈ 0.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* | ann. Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SMA cross (with the cross)** | 3,801 | **49.6%** | **−0.39** | −0.00 | **−1.12** | **−0.91** |
| Random direction (control) | 3,801 | 50.3% | +0.14 | — | +0.36 | — |

- The crossover's gross expectancy is **−0.39 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **−1.12** — statistically
  **indistinguishable from zero**, and if anything on the wrong side of it. The block-bootstrap
  95% CI on the annualised Sharpe is **[−2.39, +0.69]** (88% of resamples negative).
- It does **not beat the coin.** Cross − random = **−0.53 bps/trade**; the cross's −0.39 sits
  *inside* the random control's own seed-to-seed noise band **[−1.06, +0.23]** (20 seeds). The
  "trend filter" adds nothing a fair die doesn't already have.
- Per-instrument, no tape carries a real edge: every HAC |*t*| < 1.4 (SPY −0.13, QQQ +0.06,
  IWM −1.36, AAPL −0.80, TSLA −0.45, NVDA −0.47, ES −0.22, NQ +0.24).

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep

At ~**11.3 trades/instrument/day** (2,851/yr), a tiny per-trade cost compounds into a wall. The
gross edge is already negative, so there is **no positive break-even cost** — every bp of cost
makes a coin a *significant* loser:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | annualised |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −0.39 | −1.12 | −11.2%/yr |
| 0.5 bps | −0.89 | **−2.55** | — |
| 1.0 bps | −1.39 | **−3.98** | **−39.7%/yr** |
| 2.0 bps | −2.39 | −6.84 | — |

The edge doesn't "die at the costs line" — it was never alive. Costs just turn a flat coin into a
high-confidence way to lose ~40%/yr.

## The fixed-tick trap — how the recipe *looks* like it works

The folk version ("grab a few dollars, let the rest ride") is a small take-profit with no real
stop. It manufactures a gorgeous win-rate — and a left tail that eats it:

| Exit rule | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Symmetric 1:1 (honest) | 49.6% | −0.39 | −0.00 | −1.12 |
| TP 0.5R / SL 2R (1:4) | 80.1% | +0.40 | −2.37 | +1.20 |
| TP 0.25R / "no stop" (8R) | **93.5%** | +0.47 | **−8.03** | +1.35 |

On SPY the ~no-stop arm exits **477 take-profits, 19 end-of-day, 1 stop** — almost every trade
"wins" a sliver, the rare loss is enormous. The 93.5% hit-rate is **not** evidence of an edge:
the mean is still only +0.47 bps gross (HAC *t* = 1.35, indistinguishable from zero), the P&L skew
is **−8**, and that thin gross is buried by the same per-trade cost the symmetric arm dies to. The
win-rate is a property of the *exit asymmetry*, not of the cross.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic 5-minute tape (`data.synthetic_5m`), the same engine recovers a
crossover edge **only when bar-level momentum is planted**, and reads ≈ 0 when it isn't —
confirming the rule is a faithful momentum harvester, and that the real tape simply has no
intraday momentum at this horizon for it to harvest:

| Planted bar AR(1) momentum | cross gross (bps/trade) | beats random control? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0 (coin) | no |
| +0.10 (persistence) | positive | yes |
| −0.10 (reversion) | negative | no (wrong side) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Gross HAC *t* = −1.12 (sign wrong), no edge over a random-direction control,
  every instrument |*t*| < 1.4. There is no statistically real directional information in the
  SMA(5/10) cross at 5-minute fidelity on this tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Negative gross expectancy at ~11 trades/day → a significant loser
  (*t* = −4 at 1 bp), ≈ −40%/yr net. No positive break-even cost exists.
- **Beats a coin? — BUSTED.** The "improved dice roll" is not improved: the micro-trend adds
  nothing, and the high-win-rate version is a negative-skew illusion, not an edge.
